title: Credit Manager - Recruitment Business
company: Bond Moran Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Senior Credit Control Manager - Recruitment Business

Do you have strong credit control experience within the recruitment sector - ideally supporting a temp/contract-led business operating across multiple international markets?

If so, this is a particularly interesting opportunity to take on a broader and more strategic remit than a traditional Credit Control Manager role.

Our client is a growing international recruitment business looking to appoint an experienced Credit Control/Credit Risk & Working Capital Manager to review and strengthen the way it manages client exposure, commercial risk, funding relationships and credit-control processes across its international operations.

Importantly, this is NOT a business with a significant aged-debt problem.

The focus is much more forward-looking: understanding where risk sits, whether existing processes and structures are fit for future growth, and ensuring the business is making well-informed commercial decisions around the clients it chooses to work with and the terms it accepts.

The role will include:

Reviewing the existing credit-control function, processes, systems and team structure.

Taking a pragmatic, hands-on approach when required - getting into the detail of individual accounts, invoices, processes and issues rather than operating purely at a strategic level.

Assessing client exposure across different international markets and identifying where concentrations of risk may exist.

Working with senior stakeholders to understand whether individual contracts and client relationships represent genuinely good business from a cash, risk and working-capital perspective.

Challenging extended payment terms where appropriate, particularly where larger clients seek to impose terms that may be commercially unattractive.

Looking beyond headline revenue to consider the wider implications of client terms, payment behaviour and funding requirements.

Reviewing relationships with invoice-discounting providers across different territories and ensuring facilities remain appropriate for the business.

Understanding the interaction between client contracts, billing processes, funding arrangements and cash collection.

Identifying operational weaknesses that could create future collection or cash-flow issues even where no current debt problem exists.

Reviewing recurring administrative or contractual issues that can delay payment, create unnecessary rework or expose the business to avoidable risk.

Helping the business establish clearer controls around billing entities, contractual information, invoicing requirements and client onboarding.

Reviewing the current Credit Control team and identifying opportunities to strengthen, reshape or develop the existing team.

Improving reporting and visibility around debtor exposure, client concentration, payment terms, DSO and working-capital risk.

Identifying opportunities for automation and process improvement.

Developing a more scalable framework that can support continued international expansion.

What we're looking for

Recruitment-sector experience is particularly important for this appointment.

You'll ideally have worked within a temp or contract-led recruitment business and understand the relationship between client contracts, timesheets, payroll, billing, invoice discounting, working capital and cash collection.

International experience would be highly advantageous, particularly where you've dealt with different funding providers, client structures, currencies and payment practices across several territories.

We're looking for someone who can operate above the day-to-day ledger, but who is equally comfortable getting into the weeds when required. This is a strategic role, but it is not a purely advisory one: you'll need to be pragmatic, hands-on and prepared to work through the detail yourself in order to understand issues, challenge effectively and drive practical improvements.

You'll be comfortable asking questions such as:

Are we taking on the right type of business?

Are the payment terms commercially sensible?

Is our exposure to a particular client becoming too high?

Are our funding arrangements appropriate in each market?

Are our contracts and billing processes protecting us from avoidable delays?

Is the current team structure right for where the business is heading?

What could become a problem six or twelve months from now if we don't address it today?

You'll combine strong technical credit-control knowledge with commercial judgement, curiosity and the confidence to challenge established ways of working.

Permanent or Fixed-Term?

The current intention is for this to be a permanent appointment.

That said, our client recognises that the nature of the role may also appeal to someone who specialises in transformation, review and improvement projects.

For the right individual, they would therefore be open to considering a 12-month fixed-term contract if that structure is better suited to the candidate and the assignment.

Given the high volume of responses we receive from the combination of job boards, social media and other sources and despite our best efforts, many of our responses will be via email as we simply can't call every application - We know that's not what you want to hear but we hope you'll understand?

Short-listed candidates will obviously be contacted for this specific role, and if you haven't heard from us within a week, please assume you have been unsuccessful on this occasion.

We will keep your CV on file to contact you with regards to future roles and any other advice to help you, however if you do not wish to remain on our database, please let us know and we will obviously remove you. Alternatively, please feel free to contact us for a chat

company: Bond Moran Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
Senior Credit Control Manager

Do you have strong credit control experience within the recruitment sector - ideally supporting a temp/contract-led business operating across multiple international markets?

If so, this is a particularly interesting opportunity to take on a broader and more strategic remit than a traditional Credit Control Manager role.

Our client is a growing international recruitment business looking to appoint an experienced Credit Control/Credit Risk & Working Capital Manager to review and strengthen the way it manages client exposure, commercial risk, funding relationships and credit-control processes across its international operations.

Importantly, this is NOTa business with a significant aged-debt problem.

The focus is much more forward-looking: understanding where risk sits, whether existing processes and structures are fit for future growth, and ensuring the business is making well-informed commercial decisions around the clients it chooses to work with and the terms it accepts.

The role will include:
- Reviewing the existing credit-control function, processes, systems and team structure.
- Taking a pragmatic, hands-on approach when required - getting into the detail of individual accounts, invoices, processes and issues rather than operating purely at a strategic level.
- Assessing client exposure across different international markets and identifying where concentrations of risk may exist.
- Working with senior stakeholders to understand whether individual contracts and client relationships represent genuinely good business from a cash, risk and working-capital perspective.
- Challenging extended payment terms where appropriate, particularly where larger clients seek to impose terms that may be commercially unattractive.
- Looking beyond headline revenue to consider the wider implications of client terms, payment behaviour and funding requirements.
- Reviewing relationships with invoice-discounting providers across different territories and ensuring facilities remain appropriate for the business.
- Understanding the interaction between client contracts, billing processes, funding arrangements and cash collection.
- Identifying operational weaknesses that could create future collection or cash-flow issues even where no current debt problem exists.
- Reviewing recurring administrative or contractual issues that can delay payment, create unnecessary rework or expose the business to avoidable risk.
- Helping the business establish clearer controls around billing entities, contractual information, invoicing requirements and client onboarding.
- Reviewing the current Credit Control team and identifying opportunities to strengthen, reshape or develop the existing team.
- Improving reporting and visibility around debtor exposure, client concentration, payment terms, DSO and working-capital risk.
- Identifying opportunities for automation and process improvement.
- Developing a more scalable framework that can support continued international expansion.

What we're looking for

Recruitment-sector experience is particularly important for this appointment.

You'll ideally have worked within a temp or contract-led recruitment business and understand the relationship between client contracts, timesheets, payroll, billing, invoice discounting, working capital and cash collection.

International experience would be highly advantageous, particularly where you've dealt with different funding providers, client structures, currencies and payment practices across several territories.

We're looking for someone who can operate above the day-to-day ledger, but who is equally comfortable getting into the weeds when required. This is a strategic role, but it is not a purely advisory one: you'll need to be pragmatic, hands-on and prepared to work through the detail yourself in order to understand issues, challenge effectively and drive practical improvements.

You'll combine strong technical credit-control knowledge with commercial judgement, curiosity and the confidence to challenge established ways of working.

The opportunity

This is a chance to influence a function before problems arise rather than being brought in to repair one afterwards.

The business is growing internationally and wants to make sure its credit-control, risk and working-capital infrastructure develops at the same pace.

For the right individual, this offers genuine ownership, senior stakeholder exposure and the opportunity to shape how an important commercial function operates across an international recruitment group.

Short-listed candidates will obviously be contacted for this specific role, and if you haven't heard from us within a week, please assume you have been unsuccessful on this occasion.

title: Recruitment Resourcer
description:
Recruitment Resourcer - Blue Collar Property Services - London

27k- 30k per annum DOE + OTE Earnings

Daniel Owen is looking for an ambitious Recruitment Resourcer to join our London team, an excellent opportunity for someone looking to build a long-term career in recruitment.

Working within our Blue Collar Property Services division, you will work across a range of disciplines, including the social housing sector, building strong relationships with candidates and helping clients secure the talent they need.

Your Impact as a Recruitment Resourcer

Talent Sourcing: Seek out skilled individuals with the right qualifications, experience and career goals for temporary and permanent opportunities.

Recruitment Support: Provide recruitment and administrative support, including maintaining databases and candidate profiles.

Permanent Recruitment: Support the team with temporary and permanent blue collar construction recruitment, helping to match high-quality candidates to suitable roles.

Client Relationships: Build strong working relationships with existing clients, supporting repeat business and long-term partnerships.

The Ideal Candidate Will Be

A Proven Professional: Whether your background is in recruitment, sales, customer service or another target-driven environment, you know how to build relationships, get results and deliver a high-quality service.

Career-Focused: You are looking for more than a job; you want a long-term career where you can grow, develop and be in more control of your earnings within a supportive team.

Our Benefits Are Second to None

Fast-Track Career Development: Our directors all climbed the ladder from within, as it's important for clear progression to be visible and achievable.

Who Are We?

For over 40 years, Daniel Owen has been a leading specialist recruiter within the built environment, recognised for our honest approach, strong relationships and commitment to developing our people.

We believe recruitment is about people first. We invest heavily in training, reward success and provide the support needed for individuals to build long-term careers. As we continue to grow, there has never been a better time to join our team and make a real impact.

Ready to Take the Next Step?

Apply today to start your recruitment career with Daniel Owen. If you would like a confidential conversation about life at Daniel Owen, our Talent Acquisition team would be delighted to hear from you.

title: SEN Teaching Assistant
description:
About the Role

Are you an experienced SEN Teaching Assistant looking for your next opportunity within a primary school?

We are currently recruiting for a compassionate, proactive and committed SEN Teaching Assistant to join a welcoming primary school in Greenwich, supporting primary-aged pupils with a range of Special Educational Needs.

This role would suit someone who understands the importance of providing tailored support and can adapt their approach to help children overcome barriers to learning. You will work alongside teachers and other support staff, helping pupils develop academically, socially and emotionally while ensuring they feel supported and included throughout the school day.

The school is looking for someone who can use their initiative, build strong relationships with pupils and confidently respond to individual learning and behavioural needs. Previous experience supporting children with SEN within a primary school setting is essential. You must be comfortable supporting children who require additional guidance, encouragement and structure.

Whether you have experience as a Teaching Assistant, Learning Support Assistant or SEN Support Assistant, this is a great opportunity to further develop your experience within primary education.

Your Responsibilities
- Provide tailored 1:1 and small-group support to primary-aged pupils with additional learning needs.
- Assist pupils in accessing classroom activities and engaging with the primary curriculum.
- Support children with a variety of needs, including ASD, ADHD, SEMH and learning difficulties.
- Encourage independence, confidence and positive interactions with their peers.
- Use appropriate strategies to support behaviour, emotional regulation and classroom engagement.
- Work collaboratively with class teachers and SEN staff to ensure pupils receive consistent support.
- Adapt learning activities and resources to accommodate different abilities and learning styles.
- Recognise individual challenges and provide appropriate encouragement and reassurance.
- Support pupils during breaktimes and lunchtimes, promoting positive behaviour, safe interactions and an inclusive environment.
- Help maintain a positive, safe and supportive school environment throughout the day.

What We Are Looking For
- Previous experience supporting children with Special Educational Needs is essential.
- Previous experience working within a primary school setting is essential.
- A good understanding of different additional needs and how they can affect learning and development.
- Confident communication and the ability to build positive relationships with primary-aged pupils.
- Strong behaviour management skills and the ability to remain calm and patient when dealing with challenging behaviour.
- A flexible approach, with the ability to adapt to different pupils and classroom requirements.
- Confidence supporting pupils during lunchtime duties, including supervising children and managing behaviour in less structured settings, where required.
- A patient, proactive and caring approach, with a genuine interest in supporting children's educational and personal development.
- An enhanced DBS on the Update Service, or willingness to obtain one.

Graduates with relevant SEN experience are also welcome to apply, particularly those with degrees in Education, Psychology or related subjects who are considering a career in teaching or special educational needs.

What We Offer
- Opportunity to work within a welcoming primary school in Greenwich.
- Full-time and long-term opportunities available.
- Potential for extended or permanent placements for the right candidate.
- Valuable hands-on experience supporting primary-aged pupils with additional needs.
- Competitive daily rates depending on experience.
- The opportunity to make a meaningful difference to children's education and development.

If you have previous primary school experience, are confident supporting children with SEN and are passionate about helping pupils reach their potential, we would love to hear from you.

Safeguarding & DBS
Riley Personnel is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and vulnerable adults. All successful applicants will be subject to appropriate safeguarding and pre-employment checks, including references, qualification verification, right to work checks and an Enhanced DBS check, including a Children's Barred List check where applicable. Candidates must complete all required checks before commencing work and undertake safeguarding training as required.

title: Senior Recruitment Partner
company: Allen Lane Interim & Permanent Recruitment - Agency - Permanent
description:
Are you an experienced recruitment professional with a track record of delivering high-quality recruitment campaigns at pace? If so, this could be an exciting interim opportunity to make a real impact.

I am working with one of the UK's most respected healthcare charities, delivering advanced trauma care to critically injured patients across London. By bringing hospital-level expertise directly to the scene of emergencies, the organisation plays a vital role in saving lives and improving patient outcomes. Supported entirely through charitable fundraising, the charity continues to invest in its people, services and innovation to ensure Londoners receive world-class emergency care when they need it most.

They are looking to recruit an Interim Senior Recruitment Partner to join its People team on a 3-4 month contract paying up to £65,000 FTE (pro rata for the duration of the contract). They are looking for an experienced recruiter to support a busy period of hiring across a diverse portfolio of vacancies. This is an opportunity to work closely with senior leaders, influence hiring decisions and help secure talented individuals who align with the charity's mission and values.

The organisation is based in central London and offers hybrid working, going into the office 2 days per week. This fixed-term contract will suit a proactive and outcome focused recruitment professional who is comfortable managing multiple campaigns simultaneously while working with a high degree of autonomy.

Some of the key responsibilities of this exciting interim role include:
- Leading the end-to-end recruitment process for approximately 10 vacancies.
- Partnering with hiring managers to develop attraction and sourcing strategies.
- Managing recruitment campaigns, candidate communications and direct sourcing activity through LinkedIn and other channels.
- Screening, shortlisting and assessing candidates, whilst supporting interview and selection processes.
- Acting as a trusted recruitment advisor to senior managers and directors, providing market insight and recruitment expertise.
- Managing candidate pipelines and ensuring stakeholders are kept informed of progress, risks and opportunities.
- Supporting offer management and onboarding handovers to ensure a positive candidate experience.
- Identifying opportunities to improve recruitment processes and build future talent pipelines.

The successful candidate will bring significant end-to-end recruitment experience, ideally gained through working in house and through an agency. You will have experience managing multiple concurrent recruitment campaigns, strong direct sourcing and headhunting skills, and the ability to quickly establish credibility with senior stakeholders. Previous experience within the charity, public sector or wider purpose-led sector would be advantageous.

This role will suit a confident and resilient recruitment professional who enjoys working at pace, influencing stakeholders and delivering excellent outcomes. You will be proactive, collaborative and committed to providing an outstanding experience for both candidates and hiring managers, while supporting an organisation whose mission has a meaningful impact on people's lives.

The interview process will consist of two stages, with the second stage held in person (w/c 16th November).

For more information on this interesting and rewarding interim opportunity, please get in touch.

title: Training & Early Careers Coordinator

- Greenwich, Southeast London
